subject.title: fix(discord): disable ws 8.21.0 receiver part limits for gateway sockets

question: Should OpenClaw disable `ws` 8.21 retained-part limits entirely for trusted Discord gateway sockets while relying on the existing 16 MiB `maxPayload` cap?
rationale: The code change is narrow and well-supported, but it removes a dependency-level retained-part hardening check on a live network path, which is a maintainer security and availability tradeoff rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Accept Discord-only disable
options.body: Merge after maintainer acceptance because Discord is treated as a trusted peer and `maxPayload` remains the byte-size guard for this route.

options.title: Require finite caps
options.body: Ask for production-informed nonzero retained-part caps plus proof that they still survive the reported Discord gateway traffic.

options.title: Use alternate mitigation
options.body: Pause or reject this shape in favor of a temporary `ws` pin, upstream `ws` change, or broader Discord gateway transport strategy.

recommendation.title: Accept Discord-only disable
recommendation.body: Merge after maintainer acceptance because Discord is treated as a trusted peer and `maxPayload` remains the byte-size guard for this route.

likelyOwner.reason: This PR is assigned to `steipete`, and recent history shows ownership of the affected Discord gateway diagnostics and proxy path.
